Regular Season Career Regular Season Eugenio Suárez Bio Fullname: Eugenio Alejandro Suárez Nickname: Bolibomba Suarez Born: 7/18/1991 in Puerto Ordaz, Venezuela Debut: 6/04/2014 Married to Gpnesis...has two daughters...Enjoys reading history books, particularly related to military history...Early in his amateur career in Venezuela, his father Alejandro Felipe (who played locally as an amateur), instilled in him a cheerful, positive outlook toward life and playing baseball...throughout his playing days in the Minors and Majors, he adopted the phrase Good Vibes Only (Solo Mucha Buenas Energtas) when describing his mindset and approach to the ebbs and flows of playing baseball...During his first stint in Cincinnati and then in Seattle, he had t-shirts printed with his slogan on the front and gave them to his teammates to wear in the clubhouse during pregame 2025 Hit .228 (134-for-588) with 91 runs, 28 doubles, 49 home runs, 118 RBI, 46 walks and four stolen bases while slugging .526 with an .824 OPS in 159 games split between Seattle and Arizona...His 49 homers tied his career high (also, 2019) and ranked fifth among all Major League hitters...is one of eight players in the Majors since 2019 with multiple 40-HR seasons (Ohtani 4, Judge 3, Schwarber 3, Alonso 3, Soto 2, Acuni 2, Trout 2)...His .824 OPS was his highest since posting a career-high .930 mark in 2019 for the Reds...Belted his 300th career home run on 6/20/25 at COL off Ryan Rolison...was his second home run of the game and his third in what would be four home runs in three days (6/19-6/21)...As a member of the Diamondbacks, was named to the National League All-Star team...was his second career selection (also: 2018 with CIN)...appeared in the 7/15 All-Star Game in Atlanta and went 0-for-1 with a hit-by-pitch...made a terrific barehanded play for the first out of the ninth inning...was hit by a pitch in his second plate appearance which removed him from consideration for the end-of-the-game Home Run Derby...On 4/26 for ARI vs. ATL, went 4-for-4 with four home runs...became the 17th player in Major League history to hit four homers in a game...Produced his fourth career 100+ RBI season, becoming one of seven players in the Majors since 2018 to record 100+ RBI in at least four seasons (Devers, Soto, Alonso, Machado, Ramírez, Arenado)...Was named National League Player of the Week 4 times (3/30, 4/27, 6/22, 7/20)...became just the third player since Major League Baseball began awarding Player of the Week honors in 1973 to earn four weekly awards in a single season (J.D. Martinez in 2017 & Shohei Ohtani in 2024)...Was acquired by the Mariners from the Diamondbacks on 7/31 in exchange for INF Tyler Locklear, RHP Juan Burgos and RHP Hunter Cranton...at the time of the trade, his 36 home runs were the most of any player traded during the season in Major League history, topping Mark McGwire's 34 HR in 1997...Hit his 40th home run of the season on 8/22 vs. ARI to become the sixth player to produce a 40-home run season while playing for multiple teams within the same season...Went 4-for-4 with a double, homer, two RBI and three runs scored on 9/17 at KC, the ninth time in his career he collected a career-high four hits in a game. 2024 Hit .256 (146-for-571)/.788 OPS with 28 doubles, two triples, 30 homers, 101 RBI and 49 walks in 158 games… posted a career-best 90 runs...Received the D-backs' "Good Guy Award" by the Arizona Chapter of the BBWAA, recognizing the player who most fosters a positive relationship with the media...Since July 1, ranked among MLB leaders in RBI (first), total bases (third, 182), runs (third, 61), homers (T-3rd), XBH (fourth, 42), hits (T-5th), SLG (sixth, .617), OPS (seventh) and AVG (ninth)…Had four-hit efforts a career-best four times (previous: two games in 2018)…Recorded a career-high-tying five RBI on four occasions…had never done so more than once in a season prior...His .974 fielding pct. was sixth best among NL third basemen [min. 100 G]…His five multi-hit efforts in his first eight games as a D-back tied for second most, behind Adam Jones’ six multi-hit games...Reached base five times in a single game for the third time in his career on April 19 @ Giants, going 2-for-3 with one RBI and three walks (last: Aug. 2, 2019; 2-for-2, 3 BB @ Braves)…Hit his first home run as a D-back on March 30 vs. Rockies...Hit .353 (12-for-34)/.910 OPS with two doubles, one homer, seven RBI and three walks in his first nine games...Went 6-for-12 (.500)/1.450 OPS with two doubles, one homer, 11 RBI and two walks with runners in scoring position in his first 14 games...Hit back-to-back homers with Gabriel Moreno on June 6 @ Padres off Randy Vasquez...Reached base in a season-high 17 straight games July 24-Aug. 11…hit .338 (22-for-65)/1.098 with seven doubles, six homers, 14 RBI, four walks and one HBP...Collected his fourth and fifth career grand slams on Aug. 14 vs. Rockies and Aug. 23 @ Red Sox, respectively...Hit his 20th homer of the season on Aug. 25...Collected his fifth career walk-off hit Sept. 15 vs. Brewers (1B in 9th inn.)…Hit back-to-back homers with Josh Bell on Sept. 22 @ Brewers…marked his second back-to-back occurrence of the season...Batted .347 (35-for-101)/1.029 OPS with three doubles, nine homers, 18 RBI and seven walks over his final 26 games since Sept. 1...2024 marked his eighth straight season playing 140+ games since 2016 (excluding 2020)…Nolan Arenado and Paul Goldschmidt are the only players to have also played in 140+ games in the last eight seasons (excl. 2020)…Reached 10 years of Major League service time on July 16, 2024...Is one of three third baseman in D-backs history (10th player all-time) to collect 30+ homers and 100+ RBI in a season, with Jake Lamb/2017 (30 HR/104 RBI) and Matt Williams/1999 (35 HR/142 RBI)…Was the first D-back to reach the feat since Christian Walker in 2023 (33 HR, 103 RBI)…Became the 11th D-back all-time (17th occurrence) to record 100+ RBI in a season...In July, was one of four players in MLB with 10+ homers and 25+ RBI (also: L. Butler/OAK, 10 and 27; B. Doyle/COL, 11 and 27; B. Rooker/OAK, 11 and 30)… was the first D-back with 10+ home runs and 25+ RBI in a month since Eduardo Escobar (10 and 28) in August of 2019 [Stats Inc]…From July 1 to the end of the season, hit .325 (92-for-295)/.974 OPS with 18 doubles, 24 homers, 69 RBI and 22 walks over 78 games...From the start of July 2024, had four games with 4+ hits and four games with 5+ RBI…since RBI became an official stat in 1920, only Babe Ruth recorded at least four of each in July or later [Opta Stats]…Slugged a career-high-tying three homers on July 30, 2024 vs. Nationals (also: Sept. 5, 2020 @ Pirates)…also collected a career-high 13 total bases …became the 12th D-back ever (14th occurrence) to hit 3+ home runs in a game. 2023 Played in a career-high 162 games, hitting .232 (139-for-598) with 29 doubles (career best), 22 homers and 96 RBI in his second season with Seattle...Was one of just four players in the Majors to play in 162 games in 2023 (also: Matt Olson/ATL, Marcus Semien/TEX and Juan Soto/SD)…became the first infielder in Mariners history to play in every game (fifth overall player)...Led the American League with 11 sacrifice flies, one behind Major League leaders Cody Bellinger/CHC (12) and Will Smith/LAD (12)...Finished tied for third in MLB with 11 Outs Above Average (OAA) with Manny Machado/SD and Ryan McMahon/COL, behind Ke'Bryan Hayes/PIT (17) and Maikel Garcia/KC (13) [Source: Baseball Savant]...Tied for the fewest infield throwing errors among MLB third basemen with one (also: Maikel Garcia/KC) [min. 100 games]...Was the only MLB third baseman to record 200+ infield assists with one throwing error or fewer…his 268 infield assists were fourth-most in MLB, behind Austin Riley/ATL (287), Alex Bregman (281) and Ryan McMahon/COL (274)...Reached base safely in a career-best 21 straight games from April 2-26, hitting .284 (23-for-81) with three doubles, two homers, 15 RBI, eight walks and three HBP during the span...Homered in three consecutive games from July 17-19 to mark the sixth time accomplishing the feat in his career...Collected a RBI in a career-high 10 straight games (13 RBI) from July 28-Aug. 4 and batted .310 (13-for-42) with two doubles and two homers in the span.WBC: Selected to play for Team Venezuela in the 2023 World Baseball Classic… marked the first time representing his country at any level and batted .500 (7-for-14)/1.247 OPS with one homer and six RBI over four games while helping Venezuela reach the quarterfinals. 2022 Hit .236 (128x543) with 76 runs, 24 doubles, two triples, 31 home runs, 87 RBI and 73 walks in 150 games...Tallied 4.1 bWAR this season, 9th-most by a primary third baseman in club history (min 60% G at 3B)...his 4.1 bWAR ranked 8th among MLB third basemen in 2022...Among AL leaders, ranked T9th in HR (31), 6th in walks (73), 13th in RBI (85)...Recorded his fourth MLB season with 30+ HR and is one of 17 active players with at least four seasons of 30+ HR...has recorded 30+ HR in four of last five season with only exception being pandemic-shortened 2020 season...Led the Mariners with 31 home runs this season...became the 17th player in Mariners history to record 30+ HR in a single season...is only 2nd third baseman in club history to hit 30+ HR in a season, joining Kyle Seager (2016 & 2021)...Hit career home run #200 on May 16 at Toronto, a solo shot in the seventh inning...recorded a multi-HR game Sept. 7 vs. CWS...his first HR that game was his 1,000th career hit...Recorded 10th career multi-homer game May 6 vs. Tampa Bay, his first with the Mariners...Hit first career walk-off home run, a three-run shot in the bottom of the 11th inning July 8 vs. Toronto...Hit his 2nd walk-off home run of the season Sept. 11 vs. Atlanta, propelling the Mariners to a thrilling 8-7 win...Recorded a season-high five RBI on Aug. 19 at OAK, going 2-for-5 with two R, two HR, and five RBI in a 10-2 Mariners win...end of season, hit .247 (42x170) with 30 runs scored, five doubles, one triple, 15 home runs, 35 RBI, 22 walks...On 10-day Injured List with right index finger fracture, Sept. 17-28, 2022...Hit the 3rd of back-to-back home runs June 21 at OAK, following home runs by Julio Rodríguez and Jesse Winker...Suárez and Winker became the first duo in MLB history to take part in back-to-back home runs with two different teams, after doing so with the Reds on May 5, 2019 (via: Stats Perform). 2021 Hit .198 (100x505) with 71 runs scored, 23 doubles, 31 home runs, 79 RBI, 56 walks in 145 games. ...Trifecta - With 31 HR produced his third career 30-homer season (34 in 2018, 49 in 2019) and his fourth career 25-homer season...has tallied 30+ HR in three of his last four seasons with the only exception being the pandemic-shortened 2020 campaign (15 HR). ...Late Surge - In September & October, posted a .370 batting average with 8 doubles, 8 home runs, 13 RBI, a .460 on-base percentage and a .808 slugging percentage (1.268 OPS)...in his last 45 games beginning July 31, produced 12 HR, 25 RBI and a .975 OPS...22 of his last 35 hits were for extra bases (10 2B, 12 HR). ...A Grand - On Oct. 2 at PIT celebrated the 1,000th appearance of his Major League career with his 31st home run, a 2-run shot off Max Kranick, and a double. ...Leading Off - Made first career start batting leadoff May 25 at WSH...hit only career leadoff HR May 27 at WSH...from May 25-June 4, made nine consecutive starts batting leadoff, the only starts of his career at the top of the order. ...Ejected - Was ejected twice for arguing balls and strikes: July 31 at NYM (by Chris Segal) and Aug. 29 at MIA (Edwin Moscoso). ...500 Ribbies - Recorded his 500th career RBI June 13 vs. COL on 2-run HR off Antonio Senzatela. 2020 During the regular season led the Reds in HR and RBI...In September, led the Reds in total bases (44), HR (7) and RBI (19) in the push for their first Postseason appearance since 2013...Led the team in starts batting cleanup with 45...also made 10 starts batting third and two starts batting fifth...In Game 1 of the doubleheader on 8/2 at Det batted cleanup to snap at 100 his streak of consecutive starts batting third in the order (5/31/19 - 7/31/20)...In the 6-2 win on 9/5 at Pit became the 30th batter in Reds history to hit at least three HR in a game, accomplished for the 38th time and for the first time since Aristides Aquino did it on 8/10/19 vs Cubs...became the 10th Major League player from Venezuela to do it, the first since Det's Victor Martinez on 6/16/2016 at KC... produced a career-high five RBI for the third time and scored a career-high three runs for the 11th time...In the 5-0 win on 8/19/g2 at KC hit the 150th HR of his career (solo off Matt Harvey)...the ball remains nestled at the bottom of the Kauffman Stadium fountain...In the 7-1 win vs the Tigers on Opening Day made his 800th career appearance...Began the season 0-for-16 before he doubled off Kyle Ryan in the eighth inning on 7/28 vs Cubs...On 9/18 returned from the 3-day paternity list (daughter, Melanie Salomé)...in his absence, the Reds won both games vs the Pirates while Mike Moustakas played 3B...Did not play in spring training while recovering from 1/28/20 surgery to remove loose cartilage in his right shoulder. 2019 In a unanimous vote of the local chapter of the BBWAA, for the second straight season received the Ernie Lombardi Award as the Reds' Most Valuable Player...Received the Luis Aparicio Award as Major League Baseball's best player from Venezuela...Was the Reds' nominee for the Hank Aaron Award as the outstanding offensive player in the NL...Received 4 votes for the BBWAA's National League Most Valuable Player Award...Established single-season records for HR by a player from Venezuela and HR by a National League third baseman (49)...His 49 HR were second in the Major Leagues to NYM's Pete Alonso, who established a new Major League record for HR in a season by a rookie with 53...Ranked among the National League leaders in HR (2nd), HR ratio (11.7 AB/HR, 3rd), total bases (329, 6th), slugging percentage (.572, 8th), apps (159, T8th) and RBI (10th)...led the Major Leagues in strikeouts...In the first inning, led all Major League batters with a club record 15 HR and led the NL in slugging (.736)...Established career highs in hits, HR, slugging percentage (.572), OPS (.930), HR prior to the All-Star break (20) and HR after the All-Star break (29, club record)...tied career highs in games played and runs scored...the previous club record for HR after the All_Star break was held by Ted Kluszewski (27, 1954)...his 24 HR at Great American Ball Park fell 2 shy of Adam Dunn's 2005 single-season record...Led the Reds in games, at bats, runs, hits, total bases, HR, RBI, multi-hit games (42), 3-hit games (14) and multi-homer games (4)...Was the National League's Player of the Month for September (.337, 10hr, 18rbi, .455obp, .747slg)...was his first career monthly award and the second consecutive Reds winner, following August Player of the Month Award winner Aristides Aquino...marked the first time since George Foster (July) and Hall of Fame Joe Morgan (August) in 1976 that 2 Reds players won back-to-back Player of the Month Awards...Received votes for National League Player of the Month for July after leading the NL in HR (12), slugging percentage (.733) and total bases (66, T1st)...his 12 HR in July were the most by a Reds batter in that month since Adam Dunn hit 12 HR in July 2008...In the fourth inning on 9/18 at Wrigley Field hit his 48th HR (solo off Jon Lester) to establish a new record for HR in a season by a player from Venezuela...In the first inning on 9/25 vs Mil hit his 49th HR (solo off Jordan Lyles), a new National League record for HR in a season by a third baseman. ..Hall of Famer Tony Pérez previously held the club record for third basemen with 40 HR overall in 1970, including 39 HR while playing third base...In his last 32 apps of the season beginning 8/25 hit .349 (4 2b, 1 3b, 15hr, 25rbi, .795slg, .444obp), raising his batting average from .255 to season-ending .271...From 9/2-9/4 missed 3 starts with a bruised left hand suffered on 9/1 at StL when he was hit by a Daniel Ponce de Leon pitch...returned to the starting lineup on 9/5 vs Phi and in his last 22 apps of the season hit .338(2 2b, 1 3b, 9hr, 16rbi, .740slg, .457obp)...Produced four 2-homer games...4 times homered in at least 3 consecutive games...twice homered in 3 consecutive plate apps...In the 14-0 win on 4/9 vs Mia hit the 100th HR of his career (solo off Wei-Yin Chen)...In the 14-0 win on 4/9 vs Mia hit the 100th HR of his career (solo off Wei-Yin Chen)...On 1/28/20 had surgery to remove loose cartilage in his right shoulder, an injury suffered in a swimming pool... physical activity will be limited at the beginning of spring training...the team anticipates him to be ready to play toward the beginning of the regular season. 2018 Was voted by his peers to his first All-Star team and by the local chapter of the BBWAA the Ernie Lombardi Award as the Reds' Most Valuable Player...received two 10th-place votes from the BBWAA for the National League's Most Valuable Player Award...was 1 of only 7 players in the Major Leagues to hit at least .283 with at least 34 HR and 104 RBI (J.D. Martinez, Christian Yelich, Nolan Arenado, Manny Machado, Trevor Story, Javier Báez)...is 1 of only 4 third basemen in Reds history to produce at least 30 HR in a season (Todd Frazier, Tony Pérez twice, Deron Johnson)...was a finalist for the Louisville Slugger Silver Slugger Award...among National League third basemen ranked second in HR and RBI; third in hits, slugging and extra-base hits; and fourth in BA and on-base percentage...despite missing 16 games in April with a fractured right thumb ranked among the overall National League leaders in RBI (6th), HR (T7th), slugging percentage (8th, .526), OPS (10th, .892), BA vs LHP (9th, .320), RBI ratio (2nd, 5.1ab) and HR ratio (2nd, 15.5ab)...from 4/9-4/25 was disabled with a fractured right thumb...suffered the injury on 4/8 at Pit, when he was hit by a Jameson Taillon pitch...missed 16 games (3-13)...led the team in HR, RBI, slugging percentage (.526) and OPS (.892)...led the team in starts batting fifth in the order (54gs) but also hit second (8gs), third (7gs) and fourth (72gs)...established career highs in batting average, hits, HR, RBI, slugging percentage, OPS, total bases (277) and extra-base hits (58)...from 7/23-7/27 homered in 5 straight apps to tie the club record for consecutive games with a HR (8th player)...only Kendrys Morales (7g) and Matt Carpenter (6g) had longer home run streaks in the Major Leagues in 2018...was 1 of only 10 players in the Major Leagues to produce at least three 10-game hitting streaks (13g, 13g, 10g)...his career-high 13-game hitting streaks (6/8-6/23, 6/27-7/10) were the longest by any Reds batter in 2018...became only the third Reds batter since 2000 with at least 70 RBI (71) prior to the All-Star break, joining Ken Griffey Jr. in 2000 (72) and Brandon Phillips in 2013 (74)...in May led the Major Leagues in RBI (29) while ranking T3rd in both extra-base hits (15) and HR (8)...since RBI became an official statistic in 1920, is the only Reds third baseman ever to record at least 8 HR and 29 RBI in a calendar month...tied the franchise record for most RBI by a Reds player in his first 20 apps of a season (25)...played in his 20th game on 5/8 vs NYM and produced 4 RBI to give him 25...George Crowe (1958), Vada Pinson (1962) and Ken Griffey Jr. (2006) each produced 25 RBI in his first 20 games of those respective seasons...in the 9-game homestand from 4/30-5/9, became the first Reds batter to produce 15 RBI in a homestand since Jay Bruce had 15 RBI in 7 games from 8/8-8/14, 2011...in those 9 apps vs the Brewers, Marlins and Mets at Great American Ball Park, he hit .313 (3 2b, 3hr, .688slg, .395obp)...in the 14-3 loss on 4/6 vs Pit started at 3B but moved to SS in the eighth inning...was his first appearance at SS since 8/20/17, when he made his only appearance of that season at that position...finished the 2018 season with 3 apps at SS, including a start on 8/21 at Mil...is his only start at SS since 4/14/16 at Cubs...on 4/1 vs Wsh made the 500th appearance of his career...hit the second of the team-record 11 grand slams (5/24 vs Pit off Ivan Nova)...was his third career grand slam...between his 32nd and 33rd HR (solo HR off Alex Wood on 9/10 vs LAD, 2-run HR off Nick Kingham on 9/28 vs Pit), went 13 apps and 49 at bats, both season highs, without a home run or RBI...finished the season with 2 HR in his last 3 apps...following the season participated in MLB's Japan All-Star Series with Nippon Professional Baseball. 2017 In voting of the local chapter of the BBWAA received the Joe Nuxhall Good Guy Award...established career highs in runs, HR, RBI, walks, on-base percentage, slugging percentage and OPS...tied career highs in doubles and triples...led the team with nine 3-hit games...led National League third basemen in fielding percentage (.976)...from 7/3-9/27 produced a 71-game errorless streak, the longest of his career...committed 3 of his 9 errors over his last 3 apps of the season, including 2 errors on the same play in the Reds' final game of the year...made 153 apps and 149 starts at 3B...in the bottom of the fifth inning of the 8-1 loss on 8/20 at AtL made his only appearance of the season at SS as part of a double switch in which he replaced starter José Peraza...made a team-high 93 starts batting fifth but also hit second (6gs), fourth (14gs) and sixth (36gs)...had his best month in August, when he hit .348 with 8 HR, 20 RBI and an OPS of 1.184 (.487obp, .697slg)...from 8/9-8/25 produced a career-high 16-game on-base streak (21-52, .404, 5 2b, 6hr, 16rbi, .846slg, .556obp) that included a career-high 10-game hitting streak (8/15-8/25, 14-35, .400, 3 2b, 4hr, 11rbi, .829slg, .511obp)...produced 21 home runs at home, tied for the fourth-highest single-season total at Great American Ball Park (Adam Dunn 26, Dunn 25, Dunn 22, Jay Bruce 21)...in the seventh inning of the 8-7 loss on 5/23 vs Cle produced his first career pinch-hit HR, a 3-run shot off Bryan Shaw that tied the score at 7-7...produced three 2-homer games...following a called strikeout on 7/9 at Ari was ejected for the first time in his career (HP umpire Brian O'Nora)...on 8/17 at Cubs singled and doubled in the 9-run second inning...from 9/19-9/21 missed 3 games for the birth of daughter Nicolle. 2016 Led the club in games played, at bats and 3-hit games (11)...ranked T2nd in the National League in games played...among National League third basemen ranked sixth in HR, seventh in RBI and T6th in extra-base hits...became only the 10th third baseman in franchise history to produce at least 20 home runs in a season, joining Gene Freese (1961), Deron Johnson (1965), Tony Perez (1967, 1969-1971), Buddy Bell (1986), Chris Sabo (1990-1991, 1993), Aaron Boone (2002), Edwin Encarnacion (2008), Scott Rolen (2010) and Todd Frazier (2014-2015)...missed only 3 games all season (4/18 vs Col, 5/29 at Mil, 7/10 at Mia)...made 149 starts at 3B, 1 start at SS (4/14 at Chi) and 1 start at DH (8/29 at LAA)...in his last 69 apps of the season beginning 7/19 hit .279 (67-240, 20 2b, 5hr, 28rbi, 5sb)...from 4/6-4/10 homered in 4 of his first 6 apps of the season (9rbi), the first Reds batter with 4 homers in the club's first 6 games since Adam Dunn had 4 HR in the first 6 games of the 2004 season...produced 4 homers over 5 apps from 4/6-4/10 and 3 homers over a 4-game stretch from 5/15-5/18...in the 10-6 win on 4/7 vs Phi hit his first career grand slam (off Daniel Stumpf)...in the 11-4 win on 6/2 at Col established career highs with 2 homers and 10 total bases and tied career highs with 3 hits and 4 RBI...on 7/18 vs Atl celebrated his 25th birthday with a 2-run HR off Matt Wisler...in the 3-2 win on 9/2 vs StL produced the first walkoff hit of his career, an RBI-single off Seung Hwan Oh...from 5/19-5/30 went 0-for-28, the longest hitless skid of his career and the longest by a Reds batter since Todd Frazier went 0-for-31 from 7/26-8/7, 2013...prior to that hitless stretch hit .313 during a season-high 7-game hit streak (3hr, 8rbi)...on 10/1 vs Chi snapped an 0-for-12 skid with his first HR since 8/30 at LAA, at 29 games his longest homerless drought of the season...reached base safely in all 22 spring training apps and overall hit safely in 20 apps. 2015 Led the club in starts at SS (95) and in starts batting seventh in the order (39)...began the season at Louisville but became the club's starting shortstop on 6/11, the day after Zack Cozart suffered a season-ending knee injury...although he didn't make his season debut until 6/11, his 13 homers ranked T8th among Major League shortstops and T4th among NL shortstops...on 8/31 and 9/1 at Cubs homered in consecutive games for the only time in his Major League career...produced hitting streaks of 6, 5, 9, 8 and 7 games... produced 2 successful suicide squeeze bunts...in the 10-run sixth inning on 8/24 vs Det (12-5 win) produced a solo HR and a 2-run double in the same inning Brandon Phillips had a 2-run HR and 2-run triple...on 8/8 at Ari, his 2-run HR in the fourth inning off Robbie Ray snapped the Reds' 30-inning scoreless streak, their longest since 1989...reached base in 49 of his 57 apps for the Bats. 2014 In his Major League debut made 85 apps for the Tigers, including 81g at SS and 2g at 3B...also made 54 minor league appearances for Class AA Erie and Class AAA Toledo...on 6/4 was promoted from Toledo and made his Major League debut that day vs Tor as a defensive replacement at shortstop...on 6/7 vs Bos became the 23rd player in franchise history to produce a home run for his first Major League hit (solo off Jon Lester)...became only the fourth Tigers rookie to homer in 3 of his first 7 career starts (Alex Avila 2009, Robert Fick 1998, Frank Doljack 1930)...on 6/14 vs Min finished a single shy of the cycle...following the season played for Caracas in the Venezuelan Winter League (17g, .250, 3 2b, 3 3b, 1hr, 6rbi). 2013 Split the 2013 season between Single A Lakeland and Double A Erie, appearing in 136 games...Opened the season with Lakeland -- batted .311 (32x103) in 25 games with the Flying Tigers...Compiled a season-best 11-game hitting streak April 19-30...Had his contract transferred to Erie on May 2...Collected a season-high four hits on May 23 versus Harrisburg...Batted .253 (112x442) with 24 doubles, four triples, nine home runs and 45 RBI in 111 games with Erie. 2012 Selected to the Midwest League's mid-season all-star squad as he spent the entire 2012 season with Single A West Michigan -- tabbed the West Michigan Player of the Year...Second in the Midwest League with 147 hits, while he tied for third with 135 games played, finished fifth with 65 walks,tied for fifth with 209 total bases and tied for ninth with a .288 batting average... Led all Midwest League shortstops with 257 putouts... Compiled an 11-game hitting streak April 15-26, batting .419 (18x43) with four doubles, a home run and seven RBI... Batted .348 (31x89) with six doubles, a triple, two home runs and 12 RBI in 24 games during April... Tabbed the Midwest League Player of the Week for May 28-June 3 after hitting .643 (18x28) with four doubles, a triple and three RBI in seven games during the week... Posted a 12-game hitting streak May 28-June 9, batting .556 (25x45) with eight doubles, a triple and four RBI... Collected a season-high four hits on June 1 at Lake County -- matched the high with four hits on June 3 at Great Lakes and July 18 versus Peoria ... Earned Tigers Minor League Player of the Month honors for June after batting .366 (30x82) with 11 doubles, two triples, a home run and seven RBI in 22 games... Hit .319 (43x135) with runners in scoring position... Named the ninth-best prospect in the Tigers organization following the season by Baseball America... Saw action in two games with Caracas in the Venezuelan Winter League following the season. 2011 Assigned to the Gulf Coast League Tigers to begin the 2011 season...
